description: AFL statistics platform with PostgreSQL storage, CLI, and MCP server for LLM-powered querying

userStories.title: Research fitzRoy R package data structures
userStories.description: As a developer, I need to understand the data structures provided by the fitzRoy R package so that I can design an appropriate database schema.
acceptanceCriteria: Create docs/fitzroy-research.md documenting all key fitzRoy functions and their return structures
Document the data available from fetch_results(), fetch_fixture(), fetch_player_stats(), fetch_lineup() and other key endpoints
List all columns/fields returned by each function with data types and example values
Identify which functions cover the 2016-2025 AFL season range
Note any data quality issues, gaps, or inconsistencies discovered

userStories.title: Design PostgreSQL database schema
userStories.description: As a developer, I need a normalised PostgreSQL schema that models AFL domain entities so that data can be stored and queried efficiently.
acceptanceCriteria: Create db/migrations/001_initial_schema.sql with CREATE TABLE statements
Schema includes tables: competitions, seasons, teams, venues, matches, players, player_match_stats
competitions table has a type discriminator to support AFL and future AFLW data
All tables have appropriate primary keys, foreign keys, and indexes
Include a schema diagram or ERD in docs/schema.md
SQL file executes without errors against a clean PostgreSQL database

userStories.title: Build R data extraction scripts
userStories.description: As a developer, I need R scripts that extract AFL data from fitzRoy so that I can populate the database.
acceptanceCriteria: Create etl/extract.R that pulls match results, player stats, and team data for 2016-2025
Script exports data to CSV files in a data/raw/ directory
CSV files have consistent column naming and encoding (UTF-8)
Script is idempotent - safe to re-run without issues
Include a README in etl/ explaining how to run the extraction

userStories.title: Initialise Python project structure
userStories.description: As a developer, I need a well-structured Python project so that the core library, CLI, and MCP server can be built in a shared codebase.
acceptanceCriteria: Create pyproject.toml with project metadata and dependencies (psycopg, sentence-transformers, click/typer, fastmcp)
Create package structure: src/afl_mcp/ with __init__.py, core/, cli/, mcp_server/ subpackages
Create src/afl_mcp/core/__init__.py, db.py (database connection), queries.py (placeholder), search.py (placeholder)
Add a .env.example with DATABASE_URL placeholder
Typecheck passes with pyright or mypy configured in pyproject.toml

userStories.title: Implement database connection and migration runner
userStories.description: As a developer, I need a database connection module and migration runner so that the schema can be applied and the app can connect to PostgreSQL.
acceptanceCriteria: Implement src/afl_mcp/core/db.py with a connection pool using psycopg
Connection config reads DATABASE_URL from environment
Implement a simple migration runner that executes SQL files from db/migrations/ in order
Add a CLI command (afl-mcp db migrate) that runs pending migrations
Typecheck passes

userStories.title: Build CSV data loading pipeline
userStories.description: As a developer, I need a data loader that reads the extracted CSV files and inserts them into PostgreSQL so that the database is populated.
acceptanceCriteria: Create src/afl_mcp/core/loader.py that reads CSVs from data/raw/
Loader maps CSV columns to database schema tables with appropriate transformations
Loading is idempotent using UPSERT (ON CONFLICT) to prevent duplicates
Add a CLI command (afl-mcp db load) that runs the loader
Loader reports row counts for each table after completion
Typecheck passes

userStories.title: Implement read-only SQL query execution
userStories.description: As an AFL analyst, I want to execute SQL queries against the database so that I can explore AFL statistics flexibly.
acceptanceCriteria: Implement execute_query() in src/afl_mcp/core/queries.py
Function accepts parameterised SQL and returns results as list of dicts
Function enforces read-only access by rejecting INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE/DROP/ALTER/TRUNCATE statements
Function sets a statement timeout to prevent runaway queries
Typecheck passes

userStories.title: Add pgvector support and embedding generation
userStories.description: As a developer, I need vector embedding infrastructure so that semantic search can be implemented.
acceptanceCriteria: Create db/migrations/002_add_vector_columns.sql adding vector columns to relevant tables
Implement src/afl_mcp/core/embeddings.py with an embed_text() function using sentence-transformers (all-MiniLM-L6-v2)
Implement a generate_embeddings() function that creates embeddings for existing database records
Add a CLI command (afl-mcp db embed) that generates and stores embeddings
Typecheck passes

userStories.title: Implement semantic search
userStories.description: As an AFL analyst, I want to search for players and matches using natural language so that I can find relevant data without writing SQL.
acceptanceCriteria: Implement semantic_search() in src/afl_mcp/core/search.py
Function accepts a natural language query string and returns top-k results ranked by cosine similarity
Function supports an optional limit parameter (default 10)
Results include similarity score and the matched entity data
Typecheck passes

userStories.title: Implement filtered semantic search
userStories.description: As an AFL analyst, I want to combine semantic search with filters so that I can scope results to specific teams, seasons, or other criteria.
acceptanceCriteria: Implement filtered_semantic_search() in src/afl_mcp/core/search.py
Function accepts a query string plus optional filters: team, season_range, venue, player_name
Filters are applied as SQL WHERE clauses before vector similarity ranking
Results include similarity score and matched entity data
Typecheck passes

userStories.title: Build CLI with query command
userStories.description: As an AFL analyst, I want a CLI tool to execute SQL queries so that I can explore data from the terminal.
acceptanceCriteria: Create src/afl_mcp/cli/main.py with a CLI entry point using click or typer
Implement afl-mcp query <sql> command that executes read-only SQL
Output formats: table (default) and JSON (--json flag)
Table output uses a readable format with column headers
CLI entry point is registered in pyproject.toml [project.scripts]
Typecheck passes

userStories.title: Add search commands to CLI
userStories.description: As an AFL analyst, I want CLI commands for semantic search so that I can find data using natural language.
acceptanceCriteria: Implement afl-mcp search <query> command for semantic search
Implement afl-mcp search <query> --team/--season/--venue flags for filtered semantic search
Both commands support table and JSON output formats
Results display similarity scores alongside entity data
Typecheck passes

userStories.title: Build MCP server with SQL query tool
userStories.description: As an LLM user, I want an MCP server that exposes SQL query execution so that Claude can answer AFL stats questions.
acceptanceCriteria: Create src/afl_mcp/mcp_server/server.py using fastMCP
Expose an execute_sql tool that wraps the core execute_query() function
Tool has clear description and parameter schema for LLM consumption
MCP server can be started via afl-mcp serve command
Typecheck passes

userStories.title: Add semantic search tools to MCP server
userStories.description: As an LLM user, I want MCP tools for semantic search so that Claude can find AFL data using natural language.
acceptanceCriteria: Expose a semantic_search tool on the MCP server wrapping the core function
Expose a filtered_semantic_search tool with team, season_range, venue, player_name parameters
Both tools have descriptive docstrings explaining their purpose and parameters
Tools return structured JSON results that LLMs can interpret
Typecheck passes

userStories.title: Add schema introspection tool to MCP server
userStories.description: As an LLM user, I want a tool that describes the database schema so that the LLM can write accurate SQL queries.
acceptanceCriteria: Expose a get_schema tool on the MCP server that returns table names, columns, and types
Tool can optionally filter to a specific table
Output includes foreign key relationships
Add the same command to the CLI as afl-mcp schema
Typecheck passes
